The greatest possible length is 5.

**Odd numbers.** An odd sum of two primes must include the prime 2, so an odd number n is semi-prime exactly when n − 2 is prime. (The two primes are then different, since n − 2 is odd.)

**At most two odd numbers in a run.** Suppose a run contained three odd numbers n, n+2, n+4. Then n−2, n, n+2 would all have to be prime. One of any three numbers in steps of 2 is divisible by 3, so that number would have to equal 3. This is impossible because n > 25. So a run has at most 2 odd numbers.

**Length bound.** Odd and even numbers alternate in a run, so a run with at most 2 odd numbers has length at most 5. A run of length 5 must have the form even, odd, even, odd, even.

**A run of length 5 exists.** Take 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, all greater than 25:
- 30 = 7 + 23
- 31 = 2 + 29
- 32 = 3 + 29
- 33 = 2 + 31
- 34 = 5 + 29

Each is a sum of two different primes, so the maximum is 5.

ANSWER: 5
